title: C Programming — Pointers, Memory Allocation & Data Structures Assessment
description: Checkpoint evaluation verifying conceptual mastery across Pointer Indirection, Addresses & Pointer Arithmetic and Dynamic Memory Management & Struct Packaging.

questions.sectionTitle: Pointers, Memory Allocation & Data Structures Checkpoint
questions.prompt: If 'int32_t *p = 0x2000;', what is the value of 'p + 2' on a 32-bit integer system?
questions.explanation: Adding 2 to an int32_t pointer advances by 2 * sizeof(int32_t) = 2 * 4 = 8 bytes (0x2000 + 8 = 0x2008).

questions.sectionTitle: Pointers, Memory Allocation & Data Structures Checkpoint
questions.prompt: What is the result of dereferencing a NULL or uninitialized pointer in C?

options.text: Undefined behavior, commonly resulting in a segmentation fault process crash
A NullPointerException is thrown and caught by runtime
The variable is dynamically instantiated on the heap

questions.explanation: In C, dereferencing NULL or an invalid address triggers undefined behavior and an OS memory access violation (SIGSEGV).

questions.sectionTitle: Pointers, Memory Allocation & Data Structures Checkpoint
questions.prompt: Why should you never assign the return value of realloc() directly to the original pointer?

options.text: If realloc fails, it returns NULL and the original buffer is leaked with no reference remaining
realloc always frees the original pointer immediately
realloc only works on stack variables

questions.explanation: If realloc fails, it returns NULL while leaving the original block intact; direct assignment destroys your only pointer to that block.

questions.sectionTitle: Pointers, Memory Allocation & Data Structures Checkpoint
questions.prompt: How does sorting struct members from largest alignment to smallest affect the struct in memory?

options.text: It minimizes internal padding bytes inserted by the compiler, reducing total struct size
It makes the struct impossible to align
It converts the struct to a union

questions.explanation: Arranging struct fields by descending alignment requirements eliminates unnecessary padding holes between fields.
